words.gloss: I will not slacken my hand

literal: To do duty, a person, 'I will not slacken my hand', saying, than that greatness, dignity, possessing, there is nothing.
translation: There is no dignity greater than the greatness of a person who says, 'I will not slacken my efforts until my duty is done.'
modern: தன் கடமையைச் செய்ய ஒருவன் 'நான் என் கையைத் தளர்த்த மாட்டேன்' என்று விடாமுயற்சியுடன் கூறும் பெருமையைக் காட்டிலும் மேலான பெருமை வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet praises the relentless determination of an individual dedicated to uplifting their family and community. The phrase 'கைதூவேன்' literally means 'I will not rest my hand' or 'I will not slacken my efforts,' representing tireless work. The poet asserts that there is no greater dignity or nobility ('பீடு') in the world than the greatness ('பெருமை') of possessing such an unwavering attitude towards one's duty ('கருமம்').
